title: 12 U.S. senators, including 6 Republicans, tell Trump to drop diesel deal with Russia
summary: A dozen U.S. senators, including six of U.S. President ‌Donald Trump's fellow Republicans, called on the president on Tuesday to rescind his diesel oil deal with Russia, saying it provides Moscow…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump walks to board Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on Tuesday. A dozen U.S. senators, including six of Trump's fellow Republicans, are calling on the president to rescind his diesel oil deal with Russia, (Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: A dozen U.S. senators, including six of U.S. President ‌Donald Trump's fellow Republicans, called on the president on Tuesday to rescind his diesel oil deal with Russia, saying it provides Moscow with more fuel to finance its war on Ukraine and will ​not benefit Americans.
Letter signed by senators says deal with Russia amounts to 'gift to our adversary'

The letter added to a ​torrent of criticism of the diesel pact from Republicans as well as Democrats. It marks a shift from what had been ​Republicans' near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decisions, weeks before ⁠Nov. 3 midterm elections ⁠that will determine whether the party ‌retains control of Congress.

"Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from [Russian President ⁠Vladimi] Putin's murderous, illegal war," the lawmakers said in a letter seen by Reuters.
"This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of ‌our Allies; it should be rescinded," they said.

The letter, dated Tuesday, was signed by Republicans Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Susan Collins of Maine, Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska ​and John Cornyn of Texas, as well as six Democrats.
Trump reverses course on Russian oil sanctions

Collins, Murkowski and Tillis had joined ⁠Democrats in a joint statement on Sunday calling on Trump to "reverse course" on the ⁠deal, saying it runs counter to U.S. law barring imports of energy ⁠until ⁠Russia ends its aggression ​against Ukraine.
The Republican president was asked earlier on Tuesday about the diesel deal, but ​sidestepped a question about ⁠whether Russia could use proceeds to purchase more bombs.

Democratic Senators Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Durbin of Illinois, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Chris Coons of Connecticut also signed Tuesday's ⁠letter.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The two countries have been in a state of all-out war ever since.
